title: Aspect without grammar
title_target: Han ligger på soffan och spelar gitarr.
goal: Express what English does with -ing, "used to", "nearly" and "will have" using Swedish verb phrases: posture verbs, *hålla på att*, *brukade*, *komma att* and the perfect for the future.
bekal: you can say what someone is in the middle of doing with *sitta / stå / ligga och* and *hålla på att*
you can talk about past habits with *brukade* and about "what would happen" with *skulle komma att*
you can use the perfect for a future that is completed first (*När du har ätit…*)
wave: Go back to Unit 1: reread the dialogue “I köket på Söder” aloud, then cover the Swedish and rebuild Dian's and Elin's fronted sentences (*Elak har hon inte varit*, *Det har jag aldrig tänkt på*) from the English.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — I telefon med Oskar
dialogs.intro: A Tuesday evening in the flat on Södermalm. Dian is fighting with her methods chapter when Oskar calls from Göteborg.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Hej! Stör jag? Du låter stressad.
lines.id: Hi! Am I interrupting? You sound stressed.
lines.literal: hi! disturb I? you sound stressed.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Lite. Jag sitter och skriver på metodkapitlet, och det går trögt.
lines.id: A bit. I'm working on the methods chapter, and it's slow going.
lines.literal: little. I sit and write on method-chapter-the, and it goes sluggishly.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Vad är det för ljud i bakgrunden?
lines.id: What's that noise in the background?
lines.literal: what is it for sound in background-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det är Jonas. Han ligger på soffan och spelar gitarr. Han håller på att skriva en ny låt.
lines.id: That's Jonas. He's lying on the sofa playing the guitar. He's in the middle of writing a new song.
lines.literal: it is Jonas. he lies on sofa-the and plays guitar. he holds on to write a new song.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Och Elin?
lines.id: And Elin?
lines.literal: and Elin?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hon står och lagar mat. Hon har lovat att jag får äta när jag har skrivit klart två sidor.
lines.id: She's at the stove cooking. She's promised I can eat once I've finished two pages.
lines.literal: she stands and makes food. she has promised that I may eat when I have written finished two pages.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Hårt. Hur långt har du kommit?
lines.id: Tough. How far have you got?
lines.literal: hard. how far have you come?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: En och en halv sida. Jag höll på att ge upp i eftermiddags, men nu rullar det.
lines.id: A page and a half. I nearly gave up this afternoon, but now it's rolling.
lines.literal: one and a half page. I held on to give up in afternoon-past, but now rolls it.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Jag ringde egentligen för att höra om du kommer ner till Göteborg i maj.
lines.id: Actually, I called to find out if you're coming down to Göteborg in May.
lines.literal: I rang actually for to hear if you come down to Göteborg in May.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det beror på. När jag har lämnat in uppsatsen kommer jag gärna.
lines.id: That depends. Once I've handed in my thesis, I'd love to come.
lines.literal: it depends on. when I have left in thesis-the come I gladly.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Du brukade ju säga att du skulle vara klar i april.
lines.id: You used to say you'd be done in April.
lines.literal: you used of-course say that you would be finished in April.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det brukade jag. Nu säger jag att jag blir klar när jag blir klar.
lines.id: I used to. Now I say I'll be done when I'm done.
lines.literal: that used I. now say I that I become finished when I become finished.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Klokt. Gå och ät nu, innan Elin har ätit upp allt.
lines.id: Wise. Go and eat now, before Elin has eaten everything.
lines.literal: wise. go and eat now, before Elin has eaten up everything.

notes: **Jag sitter och skriver** — Swedish has no *-ing* form, so when it wants to stress that something is going on right now, it often borrows a posture verb: *sitta* (sit), *stå* (stand), *ligga* (lie) + *och* + the main verb. The posture verb is usually true literally — Jonas really is lying down — but its main job is to say "in progress". Both verbs always share the same tense: *Han **låg** och **spelade** gitarr.*

**Det går trögt** — *trög* (**trög**) means sluggish, slow to move. *Det går trögt* is the standard way to say that work, sales or a conversation is "slow going"; the opposite is *det rullar* or *det flyter* (it's rolling, it flows).

**Han håller på att skriva** — *hålla på att* + infinitive (**HOL-lah POH aht**) means "to be busy doing, to be in the middle of". It suggests a longer process that isn't finished: *de håller på att bygga om stationen* (they're rebuilding the station).

**Jag höll på att ge upp** — careful: in the **past tense**, *höll på att* very often means "nearly, almost": *jag höll på att missa tåget* = I almost missed the train. Context tells you which meaning is meant. Here Dian clearly did not give up.

**Skriva klart**, **äta upp** — a particle after the verb shows that the action is completed: *skriva klart* (**SKREE-vah KLAHT**, finish writing), *läsa ut* (finish reading a book), *äta upp* (eat up), *dricka ur* (drink up). This is Swedish "aspect" again, done with small words instead of verb endings.

**I eftermiddags** — the *-s* form refers to an afternoon that has already passed today: *i eftermiddags* (this afternoon, earlier), compare *i eftermiddag* (this afternoon, coming). *I morse* (earlier this morning) works the same way, and you met *i fredags* (last Friday) and *i somras* (last summer) in Swedish 102.

grammars.title: The progressive, Swedish style
body: English marks an ongoing action with *be + -ing*. Swedish usually leaves it unmarked (*jag skriver* = I write / I'm writing), but when the ongoing nature matters, it has several verb phrases to choose from.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: Vi stod och väntade i en halvtimme.
Han låg och sov när jag kom.
keep doing over a long time
Jag har gått och tänkt på det i veckor.
De håller på att renovera huset.

after: Choose the posture verb that matches reality: you *ligger och läser* in bed but *sitter och läser* on the subway. If no position is obvious, use *hålla på att* or nothing at all.

The posture verb gives the sentence a slightly drawn-out, vivid feel. In a news report you would just write *Polisen undersöker…*; in a story, *Polisen stod och undersökte bilen när…* paints the scene.

grammars.title: The perfect for a future that's already done
body: When one future action has to be completed before another, Swedish uses the perfect (*har* + supine) in the time clause, just as English does with "once I've finished". The main clause uses the present, often with a future meaning.

head: Svenska
English
rows: När jag **har lämnat in** uppsatsen kommer jag gärna.
Once I've handed in my thesis, I'd love to come.
Du får äta när du **har skrivit** klart.
You can eat when you've finished writing.
Om en vecka **har** jag **lämnat in** allt.
In a week I'll have handed everything in.

after: The last row is worth remembering: where English needs *will have* (future perfect), Swedish is happy with a plain perfect plus a time expression. *Kommer att ha lämnat in* is also correct, but heavier.
With *innan* the perfect is optional: *Gå innan Elin äter upp allt* and *…innan Elin har ätit upp allt* both work. The perfect stresses that by then it will be too late.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Söndagsmiddag hos Anna och Lars
dialogs.intro: Sunday dinner at Elin's parents' house. Lars and Anna studied in Stockholm in the 1980s and have strong opinions about what has happened to Södermalm since.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Bor ni kvar på Söder, alla tre?
lines.id: Are you all three still living on Söder?
lines.literal: live you remaining on Söder, all three?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, vi bor kvar. Jag älskar området, men hyran har blivit dyr.
lines.id: Yes, we're still there. I love the area, but the rent has gotten expensive.
lines.literal: yes, we live remaining. I love area-the, but rent-the has become expensive.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: När vi var unga brukade alla studenter bo på Söder. Det var billigt och lite slitet.
lines.id: When we were young, all the students used to live on Söder. It was cheap and a bit run-down.
lines.literal: when we were young used all students live on Söder. it was cheap and little worn.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Vi brukade sitta och prata på kaféerna vid Mosebacke till långt efter midnatt.
lines.id: We used to sit and talk in the cafés by Mosebacke until long after midnight.
lines.literal: we used sit and talk on cafés-the by Mosebacke till long after midnight.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och ingen anade att det skulle bli så populärt?
lines.id: And nobody suspected it would become so popular?
lines.literal: and nobody sensed that it would become so popular?

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Nej. Ingen kunde veta att Söder skulle komma att bli en av Stockholms dyraste stadsdelar.
lines.id: No. Nobody could have known that Söder would end up being one of Stockholm's most expensive districts.
lines.literal: no. nobody could know that Söder would come to become one of Stockholm's most-expensive districts.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Det där med gentrifiering kommer du väl att skriva om i uppsatsen?
lines.id: That whole gentrification thing — you're going to write about it in your thesis, I suppose?
lines.literal: that there with gentrification will you surely to write about in thesis-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, i sista kapitlet. Hållbart måste ju betyda att vanliga människor har råd att bo kvar.
lines.id: Yes, in the last chapter. Sustainable has to mean that ordinary people can afford to stay.
lines.literal: yes, in last chapter-the. sustainable must of-course mean that ordinary people have means to live remaining.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Där sa du något klokt. Jag har gått och tänkt på det i flera år.
lines.id: Now that's a wise thing to say. I've been turning that over in my mind for years.
lines.literal: there said you something wise. I have gone and thought on it in several years.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Lars går alltid och tänker. Han borde skriva en uppsats själv.
lines.id: Lars is always mulling things over. He ought to write a thesis himself.
lines.literal: Lars goes always and thinks. he ought write a thesis self.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: När jag har gått i pension, kanske. Mer potatis, Dian?
lines.id: Once I've retired, maybe. More potatoes, Dian?
lines.literal: when I have gone in pension, maybe. more potato, Dian?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja tack. Men sen måste jag gå hem och sitta och skriva igen.
lines.id: Yes, please. But after that I have to go home and get back to writing.
lines.literal: yes thanks. but then must I go home and sit and write again.

notes: **Bo kvar** — *kvar* means "left, remaining", and after a verb it says that something continues in the same place: *bo kvar* (still live there, stay on), *stanna kvar* (stay behind), *sitta kvar* (remain seated), *finnas kvar* (still be there). A very Swedish little word, with no single English equivalent.

**Brukade** — the past of *bruka*, "to usually do". In the present, *jag brukar* = I usually; in the past, *jag brukade* = I used to. It is followed by a bare infinitive, without *att*: *vi brukade sitta*.
**Slitet** — *sliten* (**SLEE-ten**) means worn, worn-out, shabby, and is used for clothes, furniture, people and whole neighborhoods. Here it agrees with *det*: *det var slitet*. Plural: *slitna*.
**Ingen anade** — *ana* (**AH-nah**) means to suspect, to have a hunch, to sense. *Jag anade ingenting* = I had no idea. You will meet it again in one of the best-known Swedish idioms in Unit 15.
**Det där med gentrifiering** — *det där med* + noun is a handy way of introducing a topic loosely: "that whole thing with…, that business about…". *Det där med att jobba hemifrån — fungerar det?*

**Ha råd att** — "to be able to afford to" (literally "have means"). *Jag har inte råd* (I can't afford it) is one of the most useful sentences in a country with Stockholm rents. With a noun: *ha råd **med** en bil*. And **gå i pension** (**goh ee pang-HWOON**) means to retire.

grammars.title: Looking back and looking ahead from the past
body: Two verb phrases let you tell a story about the past with the precision English gets from "used to" and "would".

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: was going to (seen from the past)
Hon sa att hon skulle vara klar i april.
would turn out to (what actually happened later)
Söder skulle komma att bli dyrt.

after: **Komma att** in the past (*skulle komma att*) is a favorite of history books and journalism: *Det beslutet skulle komma att förändra hela staden* = That decision would come to change the whole city. In everyday speech, *skulle bli* is usually enough.
Watch out for English "would" meaning a past habit ("We would sit and talk for hours"). Swedish never uses *skulle* for that: say *Vi brukade sitta och prata* or *Vi satt ofta och pratade*.

blocks.text: When Lars and Anna talk about the 1980s, they mix habits (*brukade*), ongoing scenes (*satt och pratade*) and single events (*flyttade*, *träffades*). That mix is what makes a story come alive, in Swedish as in English. The table shows the tools side by side.

head: What you want to say
Swedish tool
Example
rows: Vi satt och pratade när det började regna.
Vi höll på att missa sista tåget.

blocks.title: Time words for then and now
items: *förr* / *förr i tiden* (in the past, in the old days) — *Förr var allt bättre*, as people like to say
*på den tiden* (in those days, back then)
*numera* / *nuförtiden* (nowadays)
*fortfarande* (still) vs *kvar* (still there, remaining): *hon bor fortfarande där* = *hon bor kvar där*
*så småningom* (eventually, gradually)

sections.title: Finished or not? Small words that decide

blocks.text: Swedish has no special verb endings for "completed" versus "ongoing", but it marks the difference with particles and verb phrases. Compare each pair: the left column is a process, the right column is a result.

**Klart** and **färdigt** both mean "finished" after a verb, and are largely interchangeable: *skriva klart*, *städa färdigt*. They don't agree with anything; they are adverbs here. In speech, *klart* is the more common of the two around Stockholm.

vocab.en: to be in the middle of; (past) to nearly do
to stay on, to still live (somewhere)
to come to, to turn out to

items: Jag / höll / på / att / missa / tåget.
När / du / har / ätit / går / vi / ut.

answers: ligger — står — sitter — satt — stod — låg
Vi brukade sitta på Mosebacke. — Lars brukade läsa tidningen varje morgon. — Studenterna brukade bo på Söder. — Jag brukade dricka kaffe efter maten. — Anna brukade ringa sin mamma på söndagar.
Jag höll på att missa tåget. — När du har ätit går vi ut. — Han håller på att skriva en ny låt. — Ingen visste att det skulle komma att förändra allt. — Om en vecka har jag lämnat in uppsatsen.

Jag håller på att skriva kapitel tre. — Hon stod i köket och lagade mat. — Vi brukade prata till långt efter midnatt. — Jag höll på att ge upp. — När jag har lämnat in uppsatsen kommer jag till Göteborg. — Ingen kunde veta att det skulle bli så dyrt.
